notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch worked (Shopify storefront, robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow, User-agent * Allow: /). Discovery: New Arrivals is the one genuinely nav-linked item found in this project -- it appears in the homepage's featured-collection card ('New Arrivals' heading -> /collections/new-arrivals) and in the /pages/sitemap nav page. Opened and confirmed a real, browsable product grid (not editorial/lookbook). The collections.json 'products_count' field for this handle reads 9204, which is grossly inflated/unreliable (consistent with the known pattern on this store from the prior Home-Decor pass); the collection page's own embedded 'product_count' JSON field reads 2312, and an independent exhaustive /collections/new-arrivals/products.json id enumeration (10 pages of 250) also returned exactly 2312 unique product ids -- both agree, so 2312 is used. A second candidate, 'fresh-arrivals' (title 'Fresh Arrivals'), was found only via the full /collections.json sweep (95 collections) -- not linked from nav, header, homepage, or the sitemap page. Opened and confirmed a real product grid; embedded product_count (285) matches an exhaustive id-enumeration of 285. Checked for aliasing: enumerated both collections' full product-id sets and confirmed all 285 Fresh Arrivals ids are a strict subset of the 2312 New Arrivals ids (0 ids unique to Fresh Arrivals), so it is a genuinely narrower/'freshest' cut of the same pool rather than an unrelated listing, and also not a duplicate/alias of the full New Arrivals listing since the counts and product sets differ -- kept as a separate row per the brief's different-counts rule. Flagged for manual review because 'Fresh Arrivals' is a close synonym of the brief's listed target terms but not one of them verbatim, and because it is an orphan collection (unlinked in any navigation). No other new-in/just-in/latest/recently-added-style collection exists anywhere in the 95-collection sweep. No 'New Collection'-style editorial page was found that needed the Collection-page ambiguity test.
